literal: Without anger, the harsh words and, like enemies, the look, of those who love, seeming like strangers, are the signs.
translation: The harsh words spoken without real anger, and the hostile look resembling that of an enemy, are the subtle signs of lovers who pretend to be strangers.
modern: கோபம் இல்லாமல் பேசும் கடுமையான சொல்லும், பகைவரைப் போலப் பார்க்கும் பார்வையும், அந்நியரைப் போல நடிக்கும் காதலர்களின் குறிப்புகளாகும்.
explanation: This couplet describes the playful behavior of lovers who pretend to be distant or angry in public. The poet explains that the seemingly harsh words spoken without any real anger (செறாஅச் சிறுசொல்) and the cold glance that resembles an enemy's look (செற்றார்போல் நோக்கு) are actually the subtle signs (குறிப்பு) of lovers (உற்றார்) who are only pretending to be strangers (உறாஅர்போன்று). These outward signs of hostility are a facade to hide their deep mutual affection from others. By understanding these signs, one can perceive their true love despite their feigned indifference.
